title: Crypto Trading Signals - June 01, 2026
top_story_headline: TXFetch introduces a new way to trace crypto activity, enabling users to locate transactions from timestamps, amounts, memos, and networks across more than 10 blockchains
top_story_comment: GitHub README lists 10 networks exactly: TRON, TON, ETH, BSC, Base, Solana, BTC, LTC, DOGE and BCH. TXFetch’s edge is triage from fuzzy exchange receipts — UTC time, amount, memo — but EVM transfers are a much cleaner problem than UTXO change outputs or bridge exits, where time+amount correlation can look convincing before it’s actual attribution. Because it leans on public APIs like TronGrid, Etherscan/BscScan/Basescan, TONAPI, Helius/public RPC and mempool/blockchair-style endpoints, the bottleneck shifts from “find the hash” to API completeness, rate limits and chain-specific weirdness.
